meta.method: Read packets (stage guidance), results, .actions.md, knowledge files and, for two concrete defects, the delivered product source; no transcripts. Quotes are <=200 characters.

dimensions.name: User interface

battleship.asked: plan item 8 (DUTIES['plan'], skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py ~L1167): "UI: component, interaction and skin premises, the design guidance locator with identity, version or digest (or the named fallback), each async cue with purpose"; step-plan duty 9 via _PLAN_RECORD_INTERACTIONS: "for UI the component, interaction and skin premises, design guidance identity and version or digest (or named fallback), and the rich interactions planned" (11-step-plan.packet.md)
battleship.considered: bs:architecture.md AD-6 L53: "Choice: one component, a 10 by 10 clickable grid, a New game button, Lightning styling already on the page, no image, no font, no animation."; spec R-9 premise; step S3 task
battleship.fit: Good for scope: simple per the request, failure behaviour stated (failed call keeps previous JSON). Weak: the rendered board was never observed (51-release-verify: SYS-BOARD not-run, release accepted without the click); the in-flight overlap was not planned (see Concurrency).

chess.asked: same plan item 8 and step-plan duty 9 text (chess 08-plan.packet.md, 11-step-plan.packet.md; older wording defaults a UI to 'ambitious' without the request-ambition clause)
chess.considered: chess:architecture.md AD-9: "Choice: select a piece of the side to move, then a destination square. Promotion is a chooser with queen preselected. No drag, no animation, no keyboard path."
chess.fit: Premises fit the request. Never observed by ShipLoop: release-verify blocked twice (37, 38); the owner played it out of band and the six click sequences stay not-run.

dimensions.owner_stage: spec (consumer-visible premises) -> plan (AD) -> step-plan (UI decisions per step + check) -> release-verify (observation)
dimensions.gap: Decisions are made, but the UI card (references/platforms/ui.md) that carries overlapping-request and accessible-name rules was opened 0 times in either run; rendered verification is structurally a last-stage person check.

dimensions.name: System API interface (contracts, callers, versioning)

battleship.asked: spec item 8 (skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_prompts.py L1047): "For each service boundary specify verifiable contracts (Service discovery guidance): current authority, freshness versus revocation, incremental state, async completion"; step-plan duty 3 (L1266): "A new or changed public entry point: add a criterion that it checks its arguments and carries a contract docstring". Versioning: not in any DUTY; only coding-practices.md#schema-and-storage ("version the payload and keep old readers working through the rollout"), a pointer never opened.
battleship.considered: bs:architecture.md L27: "The grader and the board call SLBattleController.newGame(Integer) and fire(String, Integer, Integer). Both are @AuraEnabled, not cacheable, and return String."; AD-5 L49: "No version field, no migration, no retention store."
battleship.fit: Callers and shapes named, versioning decided (none). Gap: the `game` argument has no door check: SLBattleEngine.parse calls JSON.deserializeUntyped(raw) unvalidated and the controller maps only InvalidShotException, so a null or malformed string surfaces as a raw system exception. Step-plan criteria C1-C5 (11 and 25) carry no argument/contract criterion for `game`; duty 3's bullet is not gated.

chess.asked: same spec item 8 and step-plan duty 3 (chess packets)
chess.considered: chess:architecture.md ## Interfaces and boundaries: "Engine input: a FEN string and, for apply, a UCI string. Output: a FEN, a sorted List<String>, or a status word. Illegal apply throws SLChessEngine.IllegalMoveException."
chess.fit: Good: standard formats (FEN/UCI) make payload versioning N/A; illegal input has a typed contract with tests (illegalEngineMove, promotion rejections); controller error text probed (AD-8).

dimensions.gap: Caller compatibility and payload/API versioning are asked in no DUTY; the entry-point criterion is asked but unenforced.

dimensions.name: Deployment switchover (order, cutover, compatibility window, rollback, flags)

battleship.asked: release-plan item 2 (L1696): "the deploy, each access or visibility change (for example granting a role or permission, activating an app or menu entry)"; item 4 rollback; prepare item 6 (L1238): "The consumer's access: name the consumer's account or role, the entry route the plan gives them and what reaching it needs". Flags: only coding-practices.md#feature-flags (card, never opened). Plan/step-plan: no activation duty.
battleship.considered: bs:environment.md Release procedure (validate -> deploy -> assign -> confirm -> source return), L164: "Partial failure: deploy without assign leaves the tab hidden. Recovery: run the assign command."; L122: "Org rollback is outside the grant."; 08-plan summary: "share one deploy boundary and have no independently releasable state"
battleship.fit: Good order, dry-run, activation switch, partial-failure recovery and rollback limits. But the activation (permission set + assign) came from the request (01-intake S4-S5), not from analysis. Unweighed: the delivery org is the test org; after 24-test revise every test command deploys, and mutation checks put mutants on org de (24-test.result: "After a mutation run, deploy the unmutated tree again"), so cutover happened at INNER test, and release-check could only show 'present' (49). Flags/compat window: N/A, not stated.

chess.asked: same release-plan items; prepare had no consumer-access duty in this generator (10-prepare packet diff)
chess.considered: chess:architecture.md L44: "Deploy payload: Apex classes, the LWC, the tab, and the app. No profile and no permission set."; spec.md L31: "Open gap: if the deployed tab is invisible without a profile change, do not add a permission set. Record it at release verification."
chess.fit: Poor activation: Succeeded deploy, then "Page does not exist" for the user (environment.md L21); release-verify blocked twice; the owner added a permission set out of band. The request forbade grants, so this was a material requirement conflict to raise at spec, or to probe right after the first test deploy; it was deferred to the last stage. Same test-org == delivery-org mutant-deploy design (09-improve-plan review-1).

dimensions.name: Concurrency (simultaneous users, locking, idempotency, ordering)

battleship.asked: spec item 9 (L1053): "how simultaneous changes resolve"; intake item 6: "shared state across people, devices or sessions". Plan, step-plan and CODE_CRAFT: no concurrency item. platforms/ui.md (card, never opened): "With overlapping requests or changed identity, prevent superseded results and errors from replacing the latest accepted state."
battleship.considered: bs:spec.md R-9 L131: "One player, one browser. No shared game."; AD-7 pure seeded functions (replay-safe). Ordering was NOT planned (S3 task has no in-flight rule); 21-improve-implement review-1: "Found: an in-flight fire could resolve after New game and put the old game back on the board." -> commit 4c5b99b (generation token + pending guard)
battleship.fit: Two tabs: implicitly safe (each tab owns its string), not stated. Idempotency: by design. Ordering: fixed late by implement Improve, not by planning.

chess.considered: chess:spec.md R-10 L119: "Simultaneous editors are out of scope: one browser view."; L121: "Async: each click waits for the Apex return before drawing the new position."
chess.fit: Defect shipped: slChessBoard.js play() has no pending guard or stale-response check (refresh() has one), so a second destination click or New game during an in-flight applyMove lets the older response overwrite the newer state. The 'out of scope' line rode ~10 Improve handoffs unchallenged.

structure.verdict: The step plan does not make SDLC concerns explicit per item or step. Concerns that were handled well were decided upstream (spec NFR/state lifecycle, plan AD-n) from rich inline DUTY text; step-plan inherits them only as `follows` IDs. Its own concern surface is duty 9, a free-text 'Plan record' that is ungated and was skipped or compressed in all four step-plan results.

step_plan_shape.concern_surface: Duty 9: 'Plan record in the item's context or the summary (supporting reference; each step's task and criteria stay its only directive), for the topics this item touches only' - prose, no applicability/decision/evidence/check per concern
step_plan_shape.until_loop_exit_conditions: The 7 exit conditions in 11-step-plan.packet.md (L19-26) cover the result opening, steps, checks, test_commands, expectations, skills and paths; none covers duty 9 or 10

what_was_written.battleship_11: Summary has a 'Design basis kept' sentence, failure diagnostics and 'Coding selection: Apex on API 68.0, artifact is unpackaged metadata, boundary is the org deploy' with no cards selected
what_was_written.battleship_25: Revision: 'Carried over unchanged' - no plan record
what_was_written.chess_11: No Coding decision selection, no per-step failure cases, no data/migration line; UI basis by AD pointer
what_was_written.chess_17: Collapsed three steps to one; plan record not revisited

gated.spec: only R-/AD- ID preservation and the usual faults
gated.step-plan: structural fit of criteria/steps/check/test_commands/expectations/paths/follows/skill locators; nothing about any SDLC concern
gated.release-plan: assumptions, consumer_checks or consumer_checks_na, consumer_entry sources exist, HOME file written; no access/activation step required
gated.improve_planning_focus: _REVIEW_FOCUS_ITEMS + _REVIEW_FOCUS_STEPS: 7 check-validity conditions (replayable, procedure walk, weak stand-in, command runs, dropped IDs, unproven platform claim, step prerequisites); no concern-coverage condition. Every step-plan Improve pass read (Battleship 12 r1-r2; chess 12 r1-r3, 18 r1-r2) reviewed criterion/check precision only.
gated.summary: No SDLC dimension is gated at any stage.

reading any GUIDE: in plan and step-plan neither run opened coding-guidance.md, coding-practices.md, plan-record.md, behavioral-requirements.md or platforms/ui.md

recommendations.change: Replace step-plan duty 9's free-text plan record with a fixed generic concern list carried as data: plan writes per work item one row per concern (ui, api, messaging, state, migrate-before, migrate-after, switchover, concurrency, native-services, scale, security, observability, config, performance, accessibility) as {id, applies: yes|no, decision or reason, anchor (R-/AD-/HOME section), owner_stage}; step-plan maps each applies=yes row to {steps or later owner_stage, check: a test_commands criterion, case ID or procedure locator}.
